## Stage prompt +0:00:00

> Continue the saved OS and guest assembler. Prepare an application ABI so the next stage can write a compiler entirely as a guest assembly program, without changing the kernel image.
> 
> 1. Add "run N" to pass a decimal unsigned 32-bit argument to the application in w1, preserving the x0 console function ABI. Plain "run" uses zero. Keep the existing exit display.
> 2. Add "install" to copy the currently loaded program into a separate executable compiler slot and return "installed\n". Track the loaded size for load/loadfile/asm/as. If no program is loaded, print "no program\n".
> 3. Add "build NAME". Read the named source file using the disk filesystem and call the installed compiler with aligned stack, x0=console putc, x1=pointer to exact source bytes, w2=source length, x3=temporary output buffer, w4=output capacity. Compiler returns w0=generated byte length, or zero on rejection. On valid length (4..2048, multiple of four), publish the generated machine code to the usual run buffer and print "built\n"; otherwise print "build error\n" and keep the previous application. The compiler slot stays installed across builds. Report missing files, missing disk, and missing compiler clearly; use "no compiler\n" for the latter.
> 
> Preserve prior behavior, including HTTP boot and the assembler. Use the guest assembler to test with a small compiler stub that emits a runnable program based on source bytes. Run the same compiled image with two different runtime inputs. Stop the VM and save the image and concise ABI handoff notes. Use only the campaign and the provided tools.
